title: Bouncing Ball with Elasticity
description: Interactive p5.js simulation that shows how a ball's bounce height and motion change as elasticity varies between inelastic and nearly perfect collisions.
subject: Physics
Energy Transfer
learningObjectives: Relate elasticity values to the amount of kinetic energy conserved after a collision.
Predict the effect of partial energy loss on bounce height and horizontal displacement.
Compare motion profiles for highly elastic and partially elastic materials.
prerequisites: Students recognize gravity as a constant downward acceleration.
Students can describe kinetic energy qualitatively in terms of velocity.

controls.label: Elasticity
controls.description: Adjusts the coefficient of restitution between 0.30 (very inelastic) and 1.00 (perfectly elastic).

controls.label: Pause / Resume

controls.label: Restart
controls.description: Repositions the ball with a new starting velocity for fresh trials.
